title: Basic credentials with an empty password
summary: A synthetic Basic token whose decoded user-pass is a user-id followed by a colon and nothing else.
rationale: A token with an empty password has the credential shape but may hold no confidential portion; the scheme neither permits nor forbids it. The user-id alone is not shown to be secret, so the expectation is not settled by the sources.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted: RFC 7617 does not say whether an empty password is valid or confidential. Needs a maintainer decision.

sources.supports: the first colon in a user-pass string separates user-id and password from one another; text after the first colon is part of the password

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
